title: Grade XI Unit7.3 Elastic Potential Energy — consolidated 80-original-MCQ source and FBISE academic QC

crossBankAdditionalIssues.finding: Q3 identifies an apparatus solely by its external NBF Figure7.13 citation and supplies no figure or equivalent apparatus description. It is source-valid but not standalone fair.
crossBankAdditionalIssues.action: Add a teacher-reviewed original/authorized wire-and-vernier apparatus diagram with equivalent accessible text, or make the stem self-contained. Do not copy copyrighted NBF diagram into public repository.

crossBankAdditionalIssues.finding: Source introductory instructions assume ideal linear elastic behavior; individual standalone items require that condition to justify average force F/2 or U=0.5Fx, and Q35 requires the same loading path rather than just equal endpoints.
crossBankAdditionalIssues.action: Publish only an academically approved candidate with an explicit straight-line-from-zero force-extension/Hooke-law condition, or deliver an approved shared instructions panel visible to every relevant test item.

crossBankAdditionalIssues.finding: Halving area at fixed tensile force yields double extension only if both wires remain in the same linear/proportional elastic range; thin wire may leave this range.
crossBankAdditionalIssues.action: Explicitly constrain same Young's modulus and linear proportional elastic regime before scored use.

crossBankAdditionalIssues.finding: Prior batch ledgers categorized these three as direct topic candidates. Their actual tasks are graph axis/slope/proportional-line interpretation rather than calculating area/work; teacher must decide whether to count them as direct B27 summative Application evidence.
crossBankAdditionalIssues.action: Keep source items for graph prerequisites, but obtain teacher blueprint approval. If strictly limited to area/work, move to supporting and retain genuine B27 work-area scenarios.

crossBankAdditionalIssues.finding: Recognizing the Young modulus formula, identifying the circle area equation, reading a supplied stiffness slope, and choosing how to replot reversed axes are author-tagged Application in some cases. Their actual reasoning may be Recognition/Understanding.
crossBankAdditionalIssues.action: Reassess item-level cognition from the final stem and required steps; do not inflate Application labels or reclassify the original archival Word silently.

crossBankAdditionalIssues.finding: NBF p123 Example7.3 calls the 0.004m diameter r in its Given line but p124 correctly computes area using radius 0.002m. Original source area substitution is on p124. The NBF p124 summary loosely calls the stress-strain area 'strain energy'; physically that area is elastic energy density J/m^3, whereas the force-extension area has units J.
crossBankAdditionalIssues.action: Keep original corrected numeric results; annotate textbook source slips and separate total elastic energy from per-volume energy density in teaching and teacher-approved revised solutions.
